governance: Every BUILD invariant row names the EXECUTED witnesses that establish it. verify-build-bundle.py enforces exact two-way totality by introspecting the unittest test names of the four BUILD suites: every declared witness must exist, every discovered witness must appear in exactly one row, no row may be empty, and a row that declares no positive (or no adversarial) witness must name an existing row that carries it, so a shared end-to-end path is counted once and never silently missing. 2026-08-16, cohort registration: rows also carry an optional `modules` list naming the production modules the row's behaviour belongs to, and W14 level (d) requires every BUILD_MODULES entry to appear in at least one row that also states a requirement and carries a witness. For the rows that predate this change, `modules` was DERIVED MECHANICALLY from the source of each declared witness method (import aliases plus one level of module-level test-helper expansion), not asserted by hand; for the BC-* cohort rows it is stated with the row, because the row and the module were written together. W14 level (d) cannot prove replacement sensitivity - see BC-19's accepted_residual.

The known-key set is DERIVED from the committed *.fixture.json documents themselves (trust_anchor.committed_fixture_key_material), never hand-listed, and the witness proves no key literal sits in the module. BB-17_ETW_CONSUMER_LIVE_PATH_IS_NOT_A_PU.requirement: The parts of the ETW consumer that BB-16's pure-layer witnesses could not reach are exercised too, because three defects lived exactly there and each one would have surfaced only on the operator's elevated run. (1) SDK ORDINALS: the `VALUE NOT PUBLISHED` ExtType/Flags pins are re-derived from the installed evntcons.h on every run. EVENT_HEADER_FLAG_CLASSIC_HEADER was pinned at 0x0040, which is EVENT_HEADER_FLAG_64_BIT_HEADER; it is 0x0100. That constant is LIVE in `_on_event_record()`, where a false test takes a bare `return`, so the wrong pin decided the classic-CSwitch branch by pointer width and dropped every non-64-bit-header record with no fault and no count; bw54 shows that drop directly, by decoding a synthetic classic CSwitch whose header flags are written as the SDK's literals rather than as the constant under test. EVENT_HEADER_EXT_TYPE_PROCESS_START_KEY (0x000A -> 0x000D) and EVENT_HEADER_EXT_TYPE_EVENT_KEY (0x000B -> 0x000A) were wrong but DEAD (defined, never read); they are corrected so the error cannot be inherited when a reader binds them. EVENT_HEADER_EXT_TYPE_PMC_COUNTERS = 0x0008 was already correct. (2) THREAD-LIFETIME JOIN: `_decode_kernel_process_event()` hard-coded `process_start_key: None` on every thread event while `assemble_thread_lifetimes()` requires a real key, so the live thread path could never join and every physical run would have died at ETW_PROCESS_START_KEY_INVALID:None after the candidate had already executed. The key is now BOUND from the ProcessStart events the same consumer decoded, by PID and QPC interval so a reused PID cannot borrow the wrong incarnation's key, and a thread no ProcessStart explains is ETW_THREAD_START_KEY_UNBINDABLE rather than a guess or a drop. (3) LOSS COUNTERS AND THE DRAIN: `stop()` discarded the CloseTrace return and the join result and `capture()` re-queried the loss counters on the stopped session's handle. CloseTrace is now checked (ERROR_SUCCESS or the documented ERROR_CTX_CLOSE_PENDING), a pump still alive after a bounded join is an incomplete drain, both make the capture UNAVAILABLE by name instead of a count, the counters read while the session was alive are carried into the capture, and a post-stop query is refused as ETW_LOSS_QUERY_AFTER_SESSION_STOP. Teardown still runs before any drain fault is raised, so a fault never leaves a system logger running.

BB-18_THREAD_IDENTITY_IS_A_TID_AND_AN_IN.requirement: A thread is identified by its TID *and* the interval it was alive, never by either alone. Windows reuses a thread id after the thread terminates, so one TID may carry SEVERAL lifetimes in one capture provided they are DISJOINT: they are assembled, and every CSwitch observation is attributed to the lifetime whose interval CONTAINS its QPC, with an observation inside none of them refused as ETW_CSWITCH_UNATTRIBUTED_THREAD rather than joined to the nearest row. Overlapping or touching lifetimes for one TID are the impossible world and fault ETW_THREAD_LIFETIME_OVERLAPPING_REUSE (a second START at the same QPC keeps ETW_THREAD_LIFETIME_DUPLICATE_START). In the other direction, a PID is reused too, so every thread lifetime must NEST inside one live process incarnation: the binder resolves a thread event to the incarnation whose start/stop interval contains its QPC (none -> ETW_THREAD_START_KEY_UNBINDABLE, two -> ETW_PROCESS_INCARNATION_AMBIGUOUS) and the assembler refuses a lifetime that does not nest inside the member's own interval (ETW_THREAD_LIFETIME_OUTSIDE_PROCESS), which also covers thread events that arrive with a start key already set and never pass through the binder. Fault vocabulary of record (r6, SEAT1 F4): a second START at the same QPC is ETW_THREAD_LIFETIME_DUPLICATE_START; overlapping or touching lives are ETW_THREAD_LIFETIME_OVERLAPPING_REUSE; two starts with one stop is ETW_THREAD_LIFETIME_INCOMPLETE (pinned at test_mbcx01_build_measurement.py test_bw59); an unmatched stop keeps ETW_THREAD_LIFETIME_UNMATCHED_STOP.
